fault_description: SEL event 0x04 — sensor threshold crossed, lower non-critical. The earliest warning the BMC raises for a monitored sensor.
root_cause: A reading drifting out of its normal band. Informational at this severity.
solution: Identify the sensor from the event, read its current value, and trend it. Act when it reaches critical, not here — unless the drift is fast.

fault_description: SEL event 0x07 — sensor threshold crossed, lower critical. The reading is outside acceptable limits.
root_cause: A rail, fan or temperature sensor below its critical threshold.
solution: Identify the sensor and treat according to its category. A critical crossing is actionable; correlate with any other events in the same second.

fault_description: SEL event 0x0A — sensor threshold crossed, upper critical.
root_cause: A reading above its critical threshold — most often a temperature or a fan running out of range.
solution: Identify the sensor, check the category-specific cause, and correlate against inlet temperature before assuming a node fault.

fault_description: SEL event 0x11 — power supply AC input lost.
affected_parts: SC-PS2000 power supply; PDU outlet; power cord
root_cause: Loss of AC at the supply inlet. An input-side event, not a supply failure.
solution: Check the PSU input LED, trace the cord to its outlet, and confirm the outlet is live before touching the supply.

fault_description: SEL event 0x14 — power supply predictive failure asserted.
root_cause: The supply's own monitoring detected degradation ahead of an out-of-spec output.
solution: Verify the peer supply is healthy, then hot-swap the asserting unit. Do not wait for hard failure.

fault_description: SEL event 0x16 — power unit redundancy lost.
root_cause: One supply is no longer contributing — failed, removed, or without AC.
solution: Determine which supply and why. Redundancy loss on a single-feed rack means the node is one event away from dropping.

fault_description: SEL event 0x1C — fan sensor below lower non-recoverable threshold.
root_cause: A rotor stopped or slowed past recovery.
solution: Hot-swap the fan module. Confirm both rotors report in range afterwards.

fault_description: SEL event 0x1F — thermal trip, system shut down to protect hardware.
root_cause: A component exceeded its shutdown temperature.
solution: Establish why before powering back on. Check fan health, inlet temperature, baffle fitment and heatsink contact in that order.

fault_description: SEL event 0x21 — memory correctable ECC error logged with DIMM location.
root_cause: A correctable error on the identified module.
solution: Note the location, read per-DIMM counters, and decide on the pattern — one module versus a whole channel.

fault_description: SEL event 0x23 — memory uncorrectable ECC error with DIMM location.
root_cause: A hard fault on the identified module, or a controller fault if the pattern is channel-wide.
solution: Record the location before rebooting. Replace the module; escalate to board if errors follow the slot.

fault_description: SEL event 0x2B — processor internal error (IERR) asserted, with socket identified.
root_cause: An uncorrectable internal processor error.
solution: Collect the screen capture from the log bundle before rebooting, then reseat and inspect the socket.

fault_description: SEL event 0x31 — watchdog timer expired, node reset by the BMC.
root_cause: The host stopped servicing the watchdog. Points at a hung host, not at failed hardware.
solution: Investigate the host OS. A watchdog reset with no other SEL event is a software problem, not a parts request.

fault_description: SMART attribute 1 — Raw Read Error Rate. Vendor-scaled; only meaningful as a trend against itself.
root_cause: Read channel errors, most of which are corrected internally.
solution: Do not act on the raw value. Trend it against the same drive's history; act on attributes 5, 197 and 198.

fault_description: SMART attribute 5 — Reallocated Sector Count. Sectors already mapped out to the spare pool.
affected_parts: SC-HD18T SAS drive; SC-NV7T6 NVMe drive
root_cause: Media defects permanently remapped.
solution: A stable non-zero count is wear. A climbing count is a replacement. Read alongside 197 and 198.

fault_description: SMART attribute 9 — Power-On Hours. Cumulative service time.
root_cause: Not a fault indicator. Context for interpreting wear attributes.
solution: Use to judge whether a non-zero wear count is expected for the drive's age. Never a replacement trigger on its own.

fault_description: SMART attribute 187 — Reported Uncorrectable Errors. Errors that reached the host.
root_cause: Reads the drive could not correct, returned as errors.
solution: Any non-zero value is significant — this data reached the application. Replace and flag affected data.

fault_description: SMART attribute 188 — Command Timeout. Commands that did not complete in time.
affected_parts: SC-HD18T SAS drive; SC-BP24N backplane; cabling
root_cause: A drive struggling internally, or a marginal bus. A climbing count with clean media attributes points at the bus.
solution: Correlate with media attributes. Clean media plus climbing timeouts means check the backplane and cabling, not the drive.

fault_description: SMART attribute 194 — Temperature. Current drive temperature.
root_cause: Sustained high temperature accelerates wear and raises error rates.
solution: Check against airflow and blanking panels. A single hot drive in a populated bank points at that bay.

fault_description: SMART attribute 197 — Current Pending Sector Count. Sectors awaiting reallocation.
root_cause: Sectors that failed a read and have not yet been remapped.
solution: A climbing pending count reliably precedes user-visible errors. Replace rather than watch.

fault_description: SMART attribute 198 — Offline Uncorrectable. Sectors the background scan cannot read.
root_cause: Media defects found by the drive's own scan before the host hit them.
solution: Treat as pre-failure. Schedule replacement; escalate if the count climbs between reads.

fault_description: SMART attribute 199 — UDMA CRC Error Count. Errors on the interface, not the media.
root_cause: Interface signal integrity — a connector or cable problem. Not a media problem.
solution: This attribute exonerates the media. Reseat the drive, clean the bay connector, and check cabling before replacing the drive.

fault_description: SMART attribute 231 — SSD Life Left. Remaining endurance as a percentage.
root_cause: Normal NAND wear from accumulated writes.
solution: Plan replacement as the value approaches the site threshold. Not a fault — a capacity planning input.

fault_description: Xid 198 — memory rows pending remap on an accelerator module.
root_cause: Rows retired after correctable errors; the remap has not yet been applied.
solution: Drain the node and reset the module to apply the remap. Replace if rows keep being retired afterwards.

fault_description: Xid 205 — double-bit error in accelerator on-die memory.
root_cause: An uncorrectable memory error on the module.
solution: Reset and re-run diagnostics. A recurrence on the same module is conclusive — replace.

fault_description: Xid 212 — accelerator fell off the PCIe bus.
affected_parts: SC-XA400 accelerator module; SC-RS16X riser; auxiliary power
root_cause: A module, riser or power delivery failure. All three present identically.
solution: Check for a rail event at the same timestamp first. Then reseat module, riser and power leads, and swap slots to isolate.

fault_description: Xid 219 — accelerator reset required before the module can be used again.
root_cause: The module entered an unrecoverable state and needs a reset to return to service.
solution: Drain workloads, reset the module, confirm it returns healthy. Investigate the preceding error, not the reset itself.

fault_description: Xid 226 — accelerator watchdog timeout. A workload stopped responding on the module.
root_cause: Often a workload fault rather than a hardware fault.
solution: Correlate against the workload before suspecting hardware. A single module with repeated watchdog events across different workloads is the hardware case.

fault_description: Xid 233 — uncontained ECC error on accelerator memory.
root_cause: An uncorrectable error that could not be contained to one process.
solution: Record the bus ID and error, reset the module, run a memory diagnostic. A repeat on the same module is a replacement.

fault_description: Xid 241 — inter-module link error between two accelerators.
root_cause: A bridge connector or a link fault on one of the two endpoints.
solution: Reseat the bridge at both ends, then swap the bridge before suspecting either module.

fault_description: Xid 247 — accelerator power brake asserted. Clocks capped by the power subsystem.
affected_parts: SC-XA400 accelerator module; SC-PS2000 power supplies
root_cause: The node is at its power envelope, or a supply is not contributing.
solution: Check PSU redundancy and load sharing. A node running on one supply will brake its accelerators by design.
